transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

I understand your Candy washer-dryer is completely dead with no lights after last night's power cut. To guide you to the correct repair steps or part, I need the specific model number. This is usually found on a sticker inside the door rim (on the frame where the door closes) or sometimes on the back of the machine. If you can see it, please let me know what it says.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The label says CSOW 4965TWE/1-80. It's a Candy Smart Pro, about 3 years old.

Thank you for providing the model number. Since the plug fuse is fine and the machine remains completely dead (no lights or display) after a power cut, we need to verify the power path into the machine. Please unplug the machine first for safety. Then:
1. Check that the plug is firmly inserted in the wall socket.
2. Plug a known-working lamp into that same socket to confirm there is live power at the outlet.
3. Inspect the mains cable where it enters the back of the washer-dryer for any visible damage, cuts, or chafing. If the socket has power and the cable looks intact, the issue is likely an internal fault such as a blown internal fuse on the main PCB or a failed power supply unit. In that case, you will need to contact a qualified engineer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Done all three. Plug's firmly in, a lamp works fine in that socket, and the cable and plug look fine, no damage. Still completely dead though. Where do we go from here?

[Heading: Likely cause: main PCB]
The fact that it went completely dead immediately after a power cut strongly suggests that a surge has damaged the internal electronics—specifically the main PCB or the internal power supply unit. This is not something you can safely fix yourself as it involves opening the casing and working with internal high-voltage components. I recommend contacting Candy customer support or a qualified appliance engineer to replace the faulty board. If your machine is still under warranty (3 years from purchase), check your receipt and contact them first, as this repair might be covered.
